pages.h1: Camera intrinsics: from XYZ in the world to a pixel.
pages.lead: The intrinsic matrix K is the camera's own fingerprint — the part of projection that has nothing to do with where the camera is, only how it turns rays into pixels. We'll nail down exactly what K does, play with every knob, and then watch what happens to it when you crop, resize, warp, or distort the image.

pages.h1: Every entry of K, and a knob for each.
pages.lead: K is a 3×3 upper-triangular matrix with five meaningful numbers. Here's what each one physically means — and a live demo where you drag fx, fy, cx, cy, and skew and watch a 3D scene re-project in real time.

pages.eyebrow: 02 · transforms that keep K a matrix
pages.h1: Crop, rescale, flip, rotate — one rule: K′ = A·K.
pages.lead: Almost every image edit you do in pixel space is an affine transform, and an affine transform on the image just left-multiplies K. Cropping shifts the principal point; resizing scales everything; flips and rotations are the same rule with a different A. Worked formulas and a live before/after.

pages.h1: The functions that ruin the matrix representation.
pages.lead: Some operations can't be folded into any K, no matter how you choose it. Lens distortion, fisheye projection, rolling shutter, panoramas. The single litmus test that tells you in advance: does the operation keep straight lines straight?
